before: The full attention actor–critic stores 63,368 FP32 parameters, or 253,472 bytes (247.53 KiB). That count includes critic parameters that an actor-only implementation could omit. For comparison, the CC2538SF53 variant provides 512 KB flash and 32 KB RAM [22]. Flash-resident weights need not all occupy SRAM, but flash capacity alone says nothing about activation buffers, stack and protocol memory. An embedded build, linker map and peak-memory measurement are needed before claiming feasibility. The present MCU firmware handles UART parsing, frame bounds, radio FIFO access and MAC acknowledgments; it executes neither neural inference nor HMAC/Ed25519.

before: A four-second horizon, a central sink and a 60-packet burst are insufficient to establish steady-state scalability or network lifetime. After cache sorting, candidate scoring is linear in the bounded candidate count. Record expiry is more costly: each millisecond poll scans all W retained watches, giving O(W) work and O(W) memory. The frozen experiments provide neither a long-horizon reclamation policy nor measured embedded inference cost. Sections 5.6–5.7 add bounded-state tests and isolated instruction-level execution; integrated firmware costs remain unmeasured. An always-listening radio also omits the wake-up cost that evidence collection would incur under duty cycling.

before: ACK-gated censored passive feedback passed the prespecified replacement test on 30 new fixtures, improving blackhole delivery over active proofs by 4.67 percentage points. The matched controls establish neither a unique censoring effect nor an attention advantage. In the separate 180-run authenticated transport study, frozen policies operate on received wire state and local service records without an established attention benefit. Serial-interface testing corrected a receive-time error, and four emulated Cortex-M3 boards execute the compiled UART-to-radio bridge while inference and cryptography remain on the host. The 60–300 s extension exposes routing-energy exhaustion and increasing source debt. Together, these results define the benchmark’s supported feedback comparison and deployment boundary: absolute service compliance, physical-board operation, integrated on-board policy/crypto execution and measured energy remain unvalidated. The 240-run factorial extension identifies a proof-traffic delivery penalty with always-on listening, while severe loss under periodic sleeping limits transfer of that finding. Isolated Cortex-M3 execution verifies actor outputs and cryptographic primitives, not a complete embedded radio system.

The 60–300 s extension exposes routing-energy exhaustion and increasing source debt. Together, these results define the benchmark’s supported feedback comparison and deployment boundary: absolute service compliance, physical-board operation, physical on-board policy/crypto execution and measured energy remain unvalidated. The 240-run factorial extension identifies a proof-traffic delivery penalty with always-on listening, while severe loss under periodic sleeping limits transfer of that finding. Isolated Cortex-M3 execution verifies actor outputs and cryptographic primitives, not a complete embedded radio system. A four-node emulated live-path pilot now performs routing and authentication inside the MCU, including longer private-key runs. Successful delivery does not establish real-time service: receipt delays exceed the two tighter class budgets.

before: Missing forwarding evidence can reflect packet loss, contention or an unobserved transmission, making feedback design a joint problem of inference and airtime. We benchmark ACK-gated censored passive feedback against active proofs in 750 IEEE 802.15.4 runs on 30 new fixtures, with naive-passive, frozen-prior and capacity-matched policy controls. Under blackholes, delivery increases from 71.28% to 75.94%, a paired gain of 4.67 percentage points (95% interval 2.36–6.97; Holm-adjusted p=0.0161). Energy per delivered byte falls while total modeled radio energy rises slightly. The controls do not establish a unique censoring or attention advantage. A separate 180-run experiment tests frozen policies over authenticated messages and node-local records. Attention delivers 81.61% in benign conditions and 61.11% under selective dropping, without an established advantage over greedy or multilayer-perceptron routing. Serial-interface testing identifies and corrects a receive-time freshness error. Compiled UART-to-radio firmware runs on four emulated Cortex-M3 boards; neural inference and cryptography execute on the host PC. Each host-policy control delivers ten of ten packets. A further 240-run factorial study separates proof traffic from evidence handling; adding proofs reduces delivery by 6.11 percentage points with always-on listening. An isolated Cortex-M3 harness reproduces actor decisions and executes HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519. An exploratory 60–300 s extension exposes routing-energy exhaustion and increasing service debt. The contribution is a traceable comparison of feedback mechanisms and transport boundaries; the evidence does not establish sustained operation, physical-board performance, measured energy consumption or absolute deadline compliance.
